Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates markedly enlarged central pulmonary arteries (prominent hilar shadows) with abrupt tapering of the peripheral vessels ("pruning"), which are classic radiographic signs of pulmonary hypertension. This condition explains the patient's shortness of breath and right-sided heart failure symptoms like lower limb edema.
